is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles funestus s.l. and Anopheles gambiae s.l. from Cameroon (page 1, Abstract; page 2, Methods).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Reports genotyping of GSTe2 L119F in An. funestus (page 5, 8, 9-11, Fig. 7-9) and Vgsc L995F (L1014F-kdr) (page 4-5, 7, Fig. 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Fig. 7A-D reports GSTe2 L119F genotype frequencies (RR, RS, SS) for alive and dead An. funestus with sample sizes provided on the x-axis for each net treatment (e.g., IG2 alive n=45, dead n=82; RG alive n=76, dead n=43; P3.0 alive n=42, dead n=43; RS alive n=69, dead n=36). Additional breakdowns by blood-feeding (Fig. 8) and hut location (Fig. 9) with exact n are also given.

african_field_population.evidence: Anopheles funestus mosquitoes were collected as free-flying wild adults entering experimental huts in Elende, Cameroon (3°41'57.27"N, 11°33'28.46"E) between December 2021 and January 2022 (page 3, 4-5, 6).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research article evaluating bed net efficacy and resistance marker association via cone/tunnel tests and experimental hut trials.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Experimental hut collections were conducted over six weeks between December 2021 and January 2022 (page 5).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Primary study conducted in collaboration between CRID and the Cameroon National Malaria Control Programme with newly collected field data from 2021-2022.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype frequency and sample size data for GSTe2 L119F are presented in the main text Figures 7, 8, and 9.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the efficacy of standard, PBO-based (PermaNet 3.0), and dual-AI (Interceptor G2 and Royal Guard) nets in laboratory cone/tunnel assays and experimental hut trials in Elende, Cameroon. Free-flying wild An. funestus from experimental huts were genotyped for the GSTe2 L119F marker, with genotype frequencies reported for dead vs alive, blood-fed vs unfed, and room vs veranda/net.
